official_measurement_examples.name: Approved Document C scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document C covers unsuitable material, contaminants, sub-soil drainage and resistance to moisture in floors, walls and roofs.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2013 radon update
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2013 policy update aligned Approved Document C guidance with more current radon mapping so protective measures could be targeted by assessed risk.

official_measurement_examples.name: Radon map versus measurement
official_measurement_examples.fact: Radon mapping is a risk-screening input and is not a measured indoor radon result for a particular building.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning versus Building Control
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local-authority guidance distinguishes planning contamination assessment from Building Control consideration under Approved Document C.

official_measurement_examples.name: Unexpected contamination
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document C issues can arise when unexpected contamination is found during building work even if a planning condition was not imposed.

official_measurement_examples.name: Moisture resistance
official_measurement_examples.fact: Damp-proofing and moisture-resistance guidance concerns building performance and does not establish land ownership or planning status.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 local strategy
official_measurement_examples.fact: Surrey Heath's 2026 strategy describes Building Control review of contamination and ground-gas risk as distinct from planning remediation conditions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Protective measures
official_measurement_examples.fact: A requirement for radon or ground-gas protective measures does not by itself prove contamination, planning refusal or lack of development potential.

core_rules: Approved Document C compliance is not planning permission
planning permission is not proof of Part C compliance
radon map classification is not a parcel radon measurement
radon protective measures are not proof a site is contaminated
contaminated-land planning condition is distinct from Building Regulations Part C
absence of a contamination condition is not proof the ground is clean
unexpected contamination must remain an evidence issue rather than a guessed clean result
damp-proofing compliance is not land-title evidence
sub-soil drainage guidance is not sewer capacity confirmation
moisture resistance is not flood-risk planning clearance
local contaminated-land strategy is not a parcel remediation certificate
historic radon mapping must not override current evidence without date checking
ground-gas mitigation design is not proof of correct installation
Part C compliance does not create land drainage or access rights
NO_DATA must remain NO_DATA rather than no contamination or moisture constraint
no parcel ground-clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
